# A module body is a TypeScript file stored in a .vibe file (Chapter 1, Module declarations), so its directives
# must report what they report in the sibling .ts file. Keys: <directive>/<statement after it>; every position
# (arrow, function, method, nested arrow, body top level, two directives) and .vibe and .vibex behave alike.
FuzzModuleBodyDirectives expect-error/assign compiler Chapter 1 Module declarations: moving a body to a sibling .ts changes no diagnostic, but // @ts-expect-error over a type error in a declaration in a body still suppresses the error and is also reported unused (TS2578); the sibling reports nothing; lane unassigned
FuzzModuleBodyDirectives expect-error/call compiler Chapter 1 Module declarations: moving a body to a sibling .ts changes no diagnostic, but // @ts-expect-error over a call with too few arguments in a body still suppresses the error and is also reported unused (TS2578); the sibling reports nothing; lane unassigned
FuzzModuleBodyDirectives expect-error/none compiler Chapter 1 Module declarations: moving a body to a sibling .ts changes no diagnostic, but over a statement with no error // @ts-expect-error in a body is reported unused (TS2578) twice, once outside the body lines; the sibling reports it once; lane unassigned
FuzzModuleBodyDirectives expect-error/property compiler Chapter 1 Module declarations: moving a body to a sibling .ts changes no diagnostic, but // @ts-expect-error over a missing property in a body still suppresses the error and is also reported unused (TS2578); the sibling reports nothing; lane unassigned
FuzzModuleBodyDirectives expect-error/return compiler Chapter 1 Module declarations: moving a body to a sibling .ts changes no diagnostic, but // @ts-expect-error over a return of the wrong type in a body still suppresses the error and is also reported unused (TS2578); the sibling reports nothing; lane unassigned
